newsitem.title: USA: Polygamous cult leader guilty in murder scheme.
newsitem.headline: Polygamous cult leader guilty in murder scheme.

text.p: The head of the Lamb of God religious cult was found guilty Friday of murder for hire for orchestrating the killings of three former members shot to death in Texas in 1988.
Aaron LeBaron, 28, also was found guilty of racketeering and infringing on the religious beliefs of the slain Lamb of God members. He faces up to 50 years in federal prison.

LeBaron was charged with ordering the deaths of Mark Chynoweth and his brother, Duane Chynoweth, in Houston, and the nearly simultaneous killing of Edward Marston in Irving. Duane Chynoweth's 8-year-old daughter, Jenny Chynoweth, also was killed after witnessing her father's execution.

Defence attorneys during the trial contended the murders were ordered by one of Aaron LeBaron's brothers, Hebert, who -- along with three other family members -- was sentenced to life in prison for his role in the killings.

"God knows there is a mountain of evidence in this case, but the government is very thin in proving it up and applying it to Aaron LeBaron in this case," defence attorney Todd Bennett said in closing arguments late Thursday.

Following the teachings of founder Ervil LeBaron, who wrote the sect's 510-page creed while in prison in Utah, Lamb of God members believed anyone leaving the sect had to be killed before believers could inherit God's kingdom on earth.
The elder LeBaron, a self-proclaimed messenger of God, married 13 times and fathered 54 children. He died in prison in 1981.
Aaron LeBaron, who became the sect's high priest upon his father's death, was captured last year near the cult's colony in northern Mexico.
Prosecutors were searching for Tarsa LeBaron, the final family member alleged to have participated in the murder-for-hire scheme.
"This case is not over until Tarsa LeBaron is proven to be dead or she is sitting in this courtroom," prosecutor Mike Shelby said.
